story_text.value:
I built Seqora as a solo developer because I was tired of DBeaver and TablePlus, the tools I was using. None of them felt like modern tooling. DBeaver is mature, but it lacks customization and it’s slow. TablePlus puts too many limits on its free tier, like only allowing two tabs open at a time. What I wanted to do differently in Seqora was to let me visualize different objects, like indexes, partitions, etc. Another thing I found most tools lacked was a way to figure out what’s slowing down a complex query, so I built a visual EXPLAIN that shows where the time goes. I put the main focus on those two.

The next thing was being able to work on a connection visually using diagrams, so I can see how things are connected and make changes by drag and drop. Once everything is done, I can review all the SQL that will run.

I made sure the things you need for a daily driver are free, so there’s no limit on the number of queries, connections or tabs. The deep-dive parts, the object views, visual EXPLAIN and schema diagrams, are in Pro. Pro is currently $5.99/month or $49/year. It’s pre-1.0, currently at 0.4.6. It supports macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows, and Linux is coming soon.

It’s built with Tauri, Rust and Svelte. Most of the code was written with Claude Code and ChatGPT. I made the decisions and did the reviewing and testing.

I’d love it if you tried it and told me what you don’t like so I can improve it, and also what you hate about your current workbench.

story_text.value:
I've been fine tuning my own decision models lately and I've been interested in how there are no real multi-turn harnesses out there for decision models. I decided to build my own. The standard claude code style interface doesn't quite make sense with a decision model since it isn't a conversation so I built this out as a sort-of REPL inspired interface. You can also use it with the command line.

You just type facts as you get them and ask questions with a ?. The questions stick around so every new fact gets asked again and you can see the probabilities move. You can use this to chain together different series of decisions to power decision networks and graphs with nouli. You can bring your own Typesafe, OpenAI, OpenRouter, or local model to run with it.

There's some walkthroughs with real runs here: https://standing-desks.github.io/nouli/examples/

Would love feedback.

story_text.value:
I just spent hours pouring over the docs for Claude and Claude Code in order to make sense of their guardrail mechanisms and some things were very surprising!

For example, did you know that the normal/Cowork chat interface is governed by settings entirely different from the Org-level settings.json for Claude Code?

The overlap between Permissions, Sandboxed Bash tool (not to be confused with the Sandbox Runtime!) and the different operational modes (Auto, Manual, etc) can be quite confusing.

I distilled a lot of Anthropic's spaghetiffied docs to make an internal guide for my company but I'm wondering if people would like a (free) copy of it?

title.value: Ask HN: Would you be interested in a guide that explains Claude Code guardrails?

story_text.value:
I burned about $500 for this fun project: Small Python. Initial PoC used 3 resets of Codex in one session but all later development happens in Claude Code, also in one Opus 5.5 session over three days.

The outcome is a quickjs-like implementation for Python. Almost full Python 3.15 language features plus builtins are covered. No Lib/ support. Great for embedding scenarios.

No rust. Just plain C11 code.

Repo is here: https://github.com/soasme/small-python/

Ask me anything.

story_text.value:
Frontier models improve at a pace faster than the pace at which most humans are able to keep up. Not all of us are obsessed with pushing the boundaries of our agents and trying new ways to work with them. I often spend 12+ hours a day working with an LLM, and still, when I talk to people, I hear of ways of working I hadn’t thought of.

What if we could speed up that pace of learning? What if everybody shared their practices of how they are making the most of AI, and if we could learn from each other? What if AI could make that sharing happen? Could everyone catch up with AI then?

I know, it sounds dreamy, but my therapist says illusions are necessary—until some of them come true.

I built a tool that teaches your local agent to scan your sessions, spot the best practices you already use, and guide you towards the ones you haven’t discovered yet. Only names and counts reach the server. Your sessions never do.

The product has a self-consolidating catalogue of practices, MCP servers, plugins and skills.

Here’s my stack—scan (locally, all session data remains private). https://app.userrank.ai/@milstan

To spice things up and give a reason to rescan, I added rankings inspired by Foursquare (who here is old enough to remember Foursquare when it was gamified?). You can rank in the top 10 of a city, or of a field like Product.

Claude Code, 10–20 minutes on your own plan:

claude plugin marketplace add https://app.userrank.ai/plugins/marketplace.json claude plugin install userrank@userrank claude "Get my UserRank"

Codex, or a quick scan of your Claude or ChatGPT chats: https://app.userrank.ai/start

title.value: Show HN: Coding agent spots your AI practices and the ones you're missing

story_text.value:
Security should be free! I was getting mad that all the security tools that meant to guard your agents are not local and those who are, just cost a fortune.

So I’ve built Weir. You can watch you sensitive data flow, your traces and your egress tools calls.

It doesn’t stop your ADLC, it only watch it locally (no egress).

The agents you use - I’ve set a Claude code hook that stripe your known keys from tool output before the model sees them.

The agents you build - Weir plants fake keys, runs your agents flows and report every place they leaked (traces, logs, model, services). It helped me find CVE-2026-116691 in MLFlow.

Would be super happy to know what you guys think!

title.value: Show HN: Keep your credentials out of the AI agents you use and build

story_text.value:
Hi HN. Greg here.

I've been a full stack engineer for 20 years. Now all I do is shuffle messages between users, my agent fleet, our dev pipeline.. back and forth. I miss coding, solving problems, reasoning, and having an understanding and a mental model of all the work I'm juggling. But this is the job now, and there's no going back. I don't exactly feel like a 10x engineer yet, but I am for sure a 10-tab engineer.

I built (er, Claude built) Shufler to lean into my new reality. If the job is basically to shuffle things through a pipeline, why not have it be more fun.

Each row on the 3D gameboard is one of your existing terminal sessions. The columns are the steps your work moves through: Brainstorm, Plan, Build, QA, Review, Merge, Deploy. Your shipped PRs get stored in a warehouse/depot. The main things flowing across the board are your issues and PRs: each one rides along its session/row as it moves through review, CI and merge, and anything waiting on you turns red. I tend to manage several PRs within each Claude/Codex session, and this makes it easier for me to hold onto a mental model of where everything is. It's also made daily standups much easier to read-out.

I created a few skins/themes like a casino, a theme park, sky islands, a starship and a factory, because.. of course.

MacOS, works with Claude Code and Codex CLI, and cmux and iTerm (tmux should work, but I haven't tested it). It doesn't try to replace anything you already use.. just makes the orchestration more fun. You can still shift focus over to your terminal sessions when needed, use your existing skills, MCP servers, etc. There's a 3D library-building in each skin where you can specify your markdown/context folders or files, and then drag and drop to check them out by your rows/sessions.

I tried to be thoughtful on security, following patterns that I consider at work. No telemetry, and the only outside calls are your own gh calls to GitHub. Daemon only listens on localhost, and every action shows its command before it runs. MCP server is opt-in, and sending to other sessions is off by default; if you turn it on, every send is a preview plus a separate confirm you approve. Details are in the README's #safety-and-privacy, and the MCP threat model (including what it doesn't protect against) is in docs/MCP.md. To report a security issue privately (or contributions to improve), see SECURITY.md.

Demo with mock data, nothing to install at https://shufler.app

Repo at https://github.com/jgrichardson/shufler (MIT)

title.value: Show HN: Shufler: 3D gaming harness around your coding harness and dev pipeline
